name: oath
sources: Cowan, Tom. “The Pledge to the Elements.” In Patricia Monaghan, ed. Irish Spirit: Pagan, Celtic, Christian, Global. Dublin: Wolfhound Press, 2001.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: An oath was a ritual act that asked divine forces to witness a claim. The Celts placed deep trust in spoken truth, partly because they had no written tongue. A speaker made an oath by calling on gods or on elemental powers such as the Sun, the Moon, and air. Those powers would punish a speaker who lied. The common Celtic sort of oath swore by the gods of one's own people.

okr.objective: Present the oath as a Celtic ritual that calls on divine powers to verify spoken truth.
key_results: An oath calls on gods or elemental powers like the Sun and Moon.
The Celts honored spoken truth because they lacked a written language.
The powers named in an oath would punish a speaker who lied.
A common Celtic formula swore to the gods of one's own people.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
